{"self_assessment": "Impact: I set the direction for the table. I proposed a big, simple fish, an animal whose outline reads on its own, and drew it on the scratch pad within the first minute so everyone worked from the same plan. I laid the start domino and built the top curve (stroke 1) from the nose across to the tail join. That is the stretch the whole push runs through. When time was called, the fish was connected from the nose through the body to both tail lobes.

Execution: I designed the sketch around what dominoes can actually do: two gentle curves splitting from the nose, rounded corners, and a tail branching off at the right end. I built the top curve steadily and finished it ahead of the final minutes. After it was across, I inspected the join closely to check it. Once the picture was connected, I kept my hands off so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I split the work early. I asked for the bottom curve and the tail to be taken in parallel, so no one waited on the pad. I kept the table updated on my progress, and I told Tom I'd cross on my own so we wouldn't crowd each other. I also called for hands-off once everything was dark.

Leadership: I picked the animal, wrote the plan on the pad, assigned the main strokes, and set the team's pace. Near the end I made the call to stop building and protect the finished work. That kept the team focused and gave us a clean, recognizable fish at the push.", "my_share_percent": 35}
